newsitem.title: UK: British Gas down as disposal talks fail.
newsitem.headline: British Gas down as disposal talks fail.

text.p: Shares in British Gas Plc dropped in early trade on Monday after reports that the natural gas supplier will seek a reference to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) to settle a price control dispute.

The stock was also unsettled by confirmation from the company that talks had been terminated with Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc on the sale to Hydro of parts of its business in Scotland and the north of England, traders said.
The stock was down 3-1/2p at 197 by 0712 GMT.
Philip Hollobone, analyst at Williams de Broe, said the combination of the two items had hit the stock and he continued to rate it a "sell" with the dividend likely to be cut.
"The problem is a lot of people holding British Gas are sitting on big losses and brokers are tending to try to talk the shares up," Hollobone said. "But things are looking pretty grim."
British Gas shares have rallied cautiously since dropping to 171p in May, their lowest in more than five years.

Hollobone said the disposal to Scottish Hydro might have provided a welcome injection of cash but that reports suggested British Gas was unable to make progress because it could not settle other outstanding issues.

British Gas gave no reason for the ending of talks with Scottish Hydro, though a report in the Financial Times said it was unable to conclude the negotiations while under commercial and regulatory pressure.

Meantime a report in the Independent on Sunday newspaper said British Gas would refuse to accept price curbs on its TransCo pipeline business sought by regulator Ofgas, prompting a study by the MMC in the long-running dispute.
Ofgas has revised proposals originally published in May but the newspaper said there had been no breakthrough in the talks. -- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
